clearedSpotChecks.check: Arithmetic, comparison, shift, byte, sign extension, MULMOD, ADDMOD, KECCAK256, MCOPY, CALLDATALOAD and JUMPI on the official node at head 52,117,929: rerun of battery.py and targeted.py for chain 999.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I ran my own 1,600 vectors with two other seeds by eth_call with a state override on https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm on 2026-11-24. They covered MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, LT, GT, SLT and SGT at 0, 1, 2^64, 2^128, 2^192, 2^255 and 2^256-1, shift and byte indices from 0 to 257, 2^64 and 2^256-1, and 400 MULMOD cases whose three operands share the top 64 bit limb, which is the input class of the ruint 1.21.0 mul_mod fault (#681 in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/recmo/uint/main/CHANGELOG.md:18). All 1,600 matched an independent Python model. Forward and backward overlapping MCOPY of 40 bytes at offset 8 also matched. The values that TickBitmap.compress (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:16-20, signextend on the tick) and BitMath (src/libraries/BitMath.sol:12) take from these opcodes are therefore the specified ones on this node.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Jump destination analysis of the official node: does a jump to 0x5b inside push data, to any non JUMPDEST byte or past the end of code fail, and does a jump to every real JUMPDEST succeed, across 16, 32 and 64 byte borders and with a truncated trailing PUSH32?
clearedSpotChecks.note: My own probe on https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm: in the layout PUSH1 d, JUMP, PUSH2 0x5b5b, JUMPDEST, a jump to either 0x5b byte inside the PUSH2 data (offsets 4 and 5) returned 'EVM error: InvalidJump', a jump to the real JUMPDEST at offset 6 returned 1, and jumps to offset 0, 3 and 200 (past the end) failed. A jump to the 0x5b that is the only data byte of a truncated trailing PUSH32 also failed with InvalidJump. This agrees with the 21,759 target result of the research file and with the 29 bytes of value 0x5b in push data of the PoolManager bytecode staying unreachable (OPCODES.md:146).

clearedSpotChecks.check: Library versions of the public replay clients against the fixes released since: hyper-evm-sync with revm 19.2.0 and ruint 1.15.0, nanoreth with the hl-archive-node revm 29.0.1 fork and ruint 1.16.0.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Fetched on 2026-11-24: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/Cargo.lock lists revm 19.2.0, revm-interpreter 15.2.0 and ruint 1.15.0; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/Cargo.lock lists revm 29.0.1, revm-interpreter 25.0.3 and ruint 1.16.0, and its Cargo.toml lines 188-197 pin every revm crate to hl-archive-node/revm fdf9b16 with a comment naming a backport of revm PR 3805 for the inspector SELFDESTRUCT callback. The ruint CHANGELOG dates 1.21.0 to 2026-10-20 and places the mul_mod fault #681 after it, so neither replay client links it. The item says correctly that the closed validator's libraries are unknown; my MULMOD vectors with equal top limbs on the official endpoint show that the endpoint build does not carry the #681 fault, and its error string 'EVM error: InvalidJump' is the revm style. Whether the validator binary is the same build as the RPC node remains the open low lead of the research file.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Transient storage semantics on the official node (supporting the L-602 clearance of slot folding).
clearedSpotChecks.note: Added check on https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm: a contract that runs TSTORE(0,1), calls itself to run TSTORE(0,2) and then REVERT reads 1 afterwards, and 2 when the inner call stops instead of reverting; TSTORE inside a STATICCALL fails (success flag 0). The lock, the delta count and the per currency deltas that CurrencyDelta keeps in transient storage (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39) therefore roll back with a reverted frame as the code assumes. This exercises one eth_call execution only; the boundary between two transactions of one block is still shown by the archive client alone (cycle 7 critic note).
